messages.text: i have a question about the new harlo pool

Happy to help, Tom. What do you want to know about it, pool fees, how to point a unit at it, or whether it works with what you already run?

For anything firmware-side, the current details and release notes live on https://harlolabs.com/, and JD (@nullhashrate) answers Harlo OS questions fastest in our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf
do my devices have to run the harlo os on them?

Honest answer, Tom: I don't want to guess on that one. Pools are normally just a stratum address any miner can point at, but whether the new Harlo pool needs Harlo OS on the unit is something I'd rather have confirmed than assume.

I've put it to JD, who handles the firmware side, and he'll come back to you here or by email. Fastest route if you don't want to wait: post in our Discord and mention @nullhashrate, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf
Handed to the team · Harlo pool / Harlo OS requirement is not in the product facts, would not guess.
JD's been pinged and will jump in here. If you step away, the answer comes to your email on file.

this is why a ask: "At least one Harlo OS miner on this wallet must individually sustain at least 800 GH/s for one hour. Hashrate from different miners does not combine, and switching miners does not carry over qualification time. Gaps over five minutes reset that miner’s progress. Each eligible email account earns one spin credit every four hours. Multiple wallets do not increase the credits per round. No miner claim code is needed."

That text answers it for the promotion, Tom: the qualifying miner has to be running Harlo OS, and one single unit has to hold at least 800 GH/s for an hour straight, no combining across miners.

What I won't guess at is which of your units can run Harlo OS, and whether the pool itself is open to non-Harlo miners outside that promo. JD has that question already and will answer here.
i think they all can run it but are not right now. I just connected all my miners to the new harlo pool so i guess i need to move them back to my own home node.

I'd hold off before moving them back. Pointing at the pool and qualifying for the spins are two different things: your miners can very likely hash on the pool as they are, the 800 GH/s on Harlo OS is only the condition for the spin credits.

Let JD confirm that before you change anything, he's on it. If it turns out you want the spins, flashing Harlo OS on the units that support it is the move, not leaving the pool.
the spins were the main draw that made me move. I am not really wanting to put that harlo os, i can but am reluctant to do it

Fair enough, and I won't talk you into flashing anything. The terms are what they are though: no Harlo OS on the miner, no spin credits, so there isn't a workaround I can offer you.

What I'd ask JD while he's looking: whether the flash is reversible on your units, and which of yours it supports. If it goes back to stock cleanly, trying it on one unit is a low-risk test. Want me to add that to the question?
sure. I guess i can leave them on harlo pool for today and see how it goes and so you can get real users to test the backend

Appreciated, Tom, that's genuinely useful to us. I've added the two questions for JD: whether the Harlo OS flash is reversible back to stock, and which of your units it supports.

If anything looks off on the pool today, shares not landing, hashrate reading low, grab a screenshot and post it here or in Discord with @nullhashrate. Real data from a live setup beats anything we can test internally.
OR if i flash one unit to harlo os can that get me the free spins and the rest of my devices can stay on default os.

Reading those terms, yes: "at least one Harlo OS miner" is the bar, and the credits are counted per account, not per miner. So one flashed unit holding 800 GH/s for the hour should qualify you, and the rest can stay on stock.

That's me reading the same text you pasted, so let JD confirm it before you commit. Pick your strongest unit for the test, it has to hold that rate with no gap over five minutes.
do you know if my gamma 601 can run harlos os

Not off the top of my head, and I won't guess on a flash. The supported hardware list is on https://harlolabs.com/, under the Harlo OS downloads, that's the definitive answer.

I've added the Gamma 601 specifically to JD's question. Worth noting it's borderline on hashrate too: a Gamma sits around 1 TH/s, so it would need to stay above 800 GH/s solidly for the full hour to qualify.
ok thanks. BTw can you check if my creadit for the octaxe-y has bee put to my account for th eRMA

do they run harlo os  or their own closed os?

The listing doesn't state the firmware, so I'll let JD confirm rather than tell you wrong. The Hammer line is the family Harlo OS is built for, which is why I'd expect it there, but I want that confirmed before you buy on the strength of it.
